newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Cementos Caribe spearheads gains in Colombia shrs.
newsitem.headline: Cementos Caribe spearheads gains in Colombia shrs.

text.p: Colombian stocks closed higher with cement maker Cementos Caribe of the powerful Sindicato Antioqueno industrial group leading the day's gainers in Bogota and Medellin.

Medellin's IBOMED general price index closed up 0.33 percent at 13,352.06 in active trade of 2.3 billion pesos. Bogota's IBB index closed up 0.36, meanwhile, ending the day at 858.63 on lower-than-average volume of 880.7 million pesos.
Brokers said a full 80 percent of the volume in Medellin, the country's most active stock exchange, involved cross- trades in firms belonging to the Sindicato Antioqueno group.
Most shares involved in the trades ended flat but the industrial group's Cementos Caribe posted an impressive 2.55 percent gain in Bogot where it closed at 4,000 pesos.
Caribe also led winners in Medelln, where 248.42 million pesos of shares changed hands and it ended the day up 2.56 percent at 4,000 per share.
"In both cities, investors in the cement firm went out to buy in response to the company's recent low price," one broker said in a telephone interview.
He noted that Cementos Diamante, owned by Cementos Mexicanos, rose 1.38 percent in Bogot to end at 3,650 pesos.
Other gainers Friday included brewer Bavaria SA, which rose 1.52 percent in Bogot to close at 3,860 pesos, and Banco de Bogot, which ended up 1.57 percent at 5,800 pesos.
Banco Ganadero's preferential shares closed up 1.44 percent in Bogot at 210 pesos and its common shares rose 0.90 percent in Medelln to close at 278 per share.
Losers in Medelln were led by supermarket chain Cadenalco, which fell 0.55 percent to end at 900 pesos and Banco de Colombia, which closed down 1.97 percent at 446 pesos.
